{"candidate_slot":0,"current_prompt":"You are given a JSON input with a system_profile (installed products and versions) and an advisories list (each with an id, description, and affected field). Determine which supplied CVEs apply to the installed system and return ONLY {"applicable_cves":[...]} with unique IDs copied verbatim from the input. Follow these rules carefully.

1. PRODUCT MATCHING — ALIASES ARE THE SAME PRODUCT. The advisory 'affected' field uses 'vendor/product' identifiers. Inventory names may look different but refer to the SAME product: package-manager style ('jetbrains-youtrack'), repo style with underscores ('sap/solution_manager', 'hyperview/geoportal_toolkit'), or display names with spaces and capitals ('Sportsnet Sportsnet', 'jetbrains webstorm'). To compare, normalize BOTH sides: lowercase, then convert '/', '_', spaces, and all punctuation to '-', then collapse repeated dashes. Compare the full normalized string AND also the product component alone (the part after the vendor '/' in the advisory; the last components of the inventory name). Underscores in advisories are equivalent to dashes in inventory: 'solution_manager' = 'sap-solution-manager' = 'solution-manager'; 'geoportal_toolkit' = 'hyperview-geoportal-toolkit' = 'geoportal-toolkit'; 'weighbridge_automation_software' = 'uzaybaskul-weighbridge-automation-software'. 'libsoup' = 'gnome/libsoup'; 'total_security' = 'bitdefender-total-security'; 'job_portal' = 'phpgurukul-job-portal'; 'ehrd_ctms' = 'sun.net ehrd ctms' = 'ehrd-ctms'. If the product component matches after normalization, the product IS installed — do not skip it because the style differs. Do NOT match similarly-named unrelated products: 'sap-content-server' is NOT 'sap/solution_manager' or 'sap/abap_platform'; 'fortinac' is NOT 'fortiportal' or 'fortiwlm'; 'hub' is NOT 'teamcity' or 'youtrack'. Same vendor + different product component = no match.

2. VERSION COMPARISON — ALWAYS NUMERIC. Parse versions as tuples of integers split on '.', compare segment by segment numerically, never as strings. PREFIX RULE: compare the common prefix first; extra trailing segments in the inventory decide nothing once the common prefix is decided. inventory 4.12.56860.1 vs advisory = 4.12.56860 → first three segments equal → EQUAL. Trailing zeros never matter: 720.0 = 720; 7.15.0 = 7.15; 2.1.0.0 = 2.1.0; 1.0.0 = 1.0; 20230904.0 = 20230904; 4.10.0.0 vs bound 4.10.0 → equal; 9.0.18.0 = 9.0.18; 19.2 < 19.15 is FALSE (19.2 > 19.15 numerically: 2 < 15 segment-wise); 4.10 > 4.9 numerically.

3. BOUNDARIES — EXACT SEMANTICS.
- '< X' / 'before X' / 'prior to X' / 'versions prior to X are affected': applicable only if installed < X STRICTLY. If installed equals X after trailing-zero/prefix normalization (e.g. installed 1.1.1? no — installed 1.1 vs < 1.1 → NOT applicable; installed 1.0.2 vs < 1.0.3 → applicable), it is NOT applicable.
- '<= X' / 'up to and including X' / 'X and prior': applicable if installed <= X, EQUALITY INCLUDED. Installed 19.2 with '<= 19.15' → 19.2 > 19.15 → NOT applicable. Installed 2.1.0.0 with '<= 2.1.0' → applicable. Installed 9.2.8.1 with '<= 9.2.8' → prefix equal → applicable. Installed 8.5.4.0 with '<= 8.5.4' → applicable.
- '= X': applicable if installed equals X per prefix/trailing-zero rules. Multi-value equality ('= 11.1 OR = 11.2', '= 7.53'): applicable if installed equals ANY listed value. Installed 7.53.1 vs '= 7.53' → prefix (7,53) equal → EQUAL → applicable. Installed 4.12.56860 vs '= 4.12.56860' → applicable.
- Ranges '>= A and <= B': both inclusive. '>= A and < B': A inclusive, B exclusive. 'from A before B' = '>= A and < B'. Installed 3.7.1 with '>= 3.0.0 and < 3.7.2' → applicable. Installed 8.11.1.1 with '>= 8.10.0 and < 8.14.0' → applicable; with '>= 8.4.0 and < 8.11.1' → 8.11.1.1 vs 8.11.1 prefix equal → equal, NOT < bound → NOT applicable.
- LOWER BOUNDS MATTER: '>= A and < B' is NOT satisfied when installed < A, even though installed < B. Installed 7.0.1 with '>= 7.0.0 and < 7.17.16' → 7.0.1 >= 7.0.0 → applicable. Installed 7.0.1 with '>= 8.0.0 and < 8.11.2' → below lower bound → NOT applicable.
- OR of multiple conditions/ranges (e.g. 'fortiwlm: >= 8.5.0 and <= 8.5.4 OR fortiwlm: >= 8.6.0 and <= 8.6.5'; 'nozominetworks/cmc: < 22.6.3 OR guardian: >= 23.0.0 and < 23.1.0'): the advisory applies if ANY single condition is satisfied for a matching installed product. Installed guardian 22.6.2.0 with 'guardian < 22.6.3' → applicable. Installed 22.6.3.1 with '< 22.6.3' → not <, but check every other OR branch before rejecting.

4. WHERE TO READ BOUNDS. The structured 'affected' field is authoritative. Descriptions often restate bounds in prose ('before 3.0.0', 'from 1.0.0.95 before 1.0.0.100', 'versions 5.5.3 and prior', 'up to and including 2.1.0', 'version 19.15 and prior versions', 'up to but excluding X'). Use both; when they conflict, the structured field wins.

5. COMMON MISTAKES TO AVOID.
- MISSING APPLICABLE CVEs IS THE MOST COSTLY ERROR. Re-check EVERY advisory whose product matches the inventory after normalization, especially when: the installed version is strictly below the fixed version (typical applicable case: YouTrack 2023.3.22269 < 2024.3.47707 → applicable; aybs 1.0.2 < 1.0.3 → applicable; snapcenter 4.10 with '>= 3.0 and < 4.9' → 4.10 > 4.9 → NOT applicable); the installed version sits exactly ON an inclusive bound ('=' or '<=' with trailing zeros, prefix-equal versions); the inventory name uses a different alias style (dashes vs slashes vs underscores vs spaces) than the advisory. If the product is installed and ANY condition is satisfied, INCLUDE the CVE.
- Do NOT include a CVE whose product is not actually installed, even if its description mentions that product or other products in prose (e.g. advisories for Bitdefender, osCommerce, FortiPortal, TeamCity, Apache Superset when only YouTrack/Kibana/etc. are installed). Prose mentions do not count — only inventory entries do.
- Do NOT include a CVE when the installed version is outside the range: installed equals an exclusive upper bound ('< X' with installed == X after normalization) → NOT applicable; installed above the bound → NOT applicable; installed below a range's lower bound ('>= A') → NOT applicable even if it is also < the upper bound.
- Do not compare version strings lexicographically: 19.2 vs 19.15 → 19.2 is GREATER (2 < 15 as integers); 4.10 vs 4.9 → 4.10 is GREATER; 20230914 vs 20230913 → greater.

6. PROCEDURE. For each advisory: (a) split 'affected' on ' OR ' and extract each product + version condition; (b) normalize names (slashes, underscores, dashes, spaces, punctuation → '-') and find a matching installed product by full name OR product component; (c) if found, compare the installed version numerically against EACH condition, honoring prefix-equality and trailing-zero rules; (d) if ANY condition is satisfied, include the advisory's id verbatim. After processing all advisories, deduplicate IDs. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Output ONLY the JSON object, no
